note_tweet.text:
To be honest, among Chinese LPL viewers, BLG fans and TES fans have basically reached the point where they can no longer have a proper conversation.

The biggest pain point for BLG fans is losing to T1, losing to Gen.G, losing MSI, or missing out on a Worlds title — international tournaments like that. If you use LCK teams to mock BLG fans, it really does hurt them.

But TES fans are different. They never seriously believed TES could beat LCK teams in the first place. Their biggest hope is simply to cling onto BLG and make people think TES and BLG are teams on the same level.

What BLG fans talk about every day is stuff like “never forget the warning signs,” “the Golden Road,” and international championships. Their goals are all about winning on the international stage.

I have never seen anyone say BLG’s goal is to beat TES.

Meanwhile, TES fans do nothing but repeat the same lines every day: “we beat you head-to-head,” “you finished top 16,” and that is basically all they have.

Because deep down, they themselves do not believe TES can beat T1, Gen.G, or HLE — let alone win an international title.

So all they can do is stick themselves onto BLG and borrow a little sense of presence from them.

note_tweet.text:
I really didn’t want to write this, but it feels necessary.

What does TES’s performance at this tournament actually tell us?

1、APAC teams have defeated an LPL team in a BO5 for the first time in history.

2、After nine years of perseverance, a Vietnamese team has finally beaten a Major Region team in a BO5 at an international event.

3、TES has now finished 8th once and 6th once — both of LPL’s worst-ever MSI placements were recorded by TES.

4、TES also becomes the first LPL team to fail to win a single series at an official international event.

5、This is also the first time an LPL team has lost a BO5 to a Vietnamese team in an international tournament.

6、For the first time, a Vietnamese team has won a BO5 in the main stage of an international event.

7、JackeyLove becomes the first player in history to lose a BO5 against all five major regions at international events.
